A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dual-Anchoring work and are fully readable. The main paper and references are identical apart from the arXiv version/date stamp. v2 omits v1's supplementary Sections A–B, Tables S1–S2 and Figures S1–S4; this is a verified document omission, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original R2R-CE and RxR-CE experiments, component ablations, data-quality evaluations and robot demonstrations. Supplementary Section B also reports a human evaluation of generated progress and memory-grounding analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, component ablations, trajectory-length analysis, data-quality evaluations and real-world demonstration in Section 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same backbone, instruction-progress supervision, SAM-based landmark reconstruction, losses and two-stage training procedure. Removing supplementary implementation descriptions does not establish a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: The training sources in Table 1, R2R-CE/RxR-CE benchmarks and indoor robot-navigation coverage remain unchanged. The omitted progress, memory and trajectory studies examine existing navigation tasks and environments rather than establish different dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Removing Table S2 eliminates the generated-progress comparison against the Baseline described as lacking Instruction Progress Anchoring and the offline PAG upper bound. PAG remains part of data generation. The main navigation comparator set and component/data-quality controls are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section B.1's evaluation protocol disappears, including binary progress-correctness judgments by 10 AI researchers alongside automated HR/LCS assessment. Section B.3's feature-similarity probing procedure is also omitted. Retained benchmark splits and evaluation settings are unchanged; missing training hyperparameters represent lost disclosure.

E4.justification: v2 removes direct human and automated validation of inference-time progress grounding, the retrospective landmark-similarity diagnostic, and additional simulated and real-world case studies in Sections B.1–B.4. This substantially reduces evidence testing both anchoring mechanisms, although the main component ablations and trajectory-length analysis remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. The removed ten-researcher evaluation panel describes the evaluation design, not an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: An entire set of direct grounding results disappears. Table S2 reports baseline/ours/PAG HR of 19.2/7.62/6.87%, LCS of 1.45/3.89/4.12 and human correctness of 29.3/86.7/93.2%. Figure S3's landmark-matching findings and additional navigation outcomes are also removed. Main benchmark scores remain identical; Table S2's SR/SPL values already appear in retained Tables 2–3.

T1.justification: The task formulation, spatial-query decoder equations and loss definitions in Section 3 and Equations 1–5 are unchanged. The omitted supplement contains implementation and empirical analyses, without additional theorems, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same state-drift diagnosis, two anchoring contributions, dataset-scale claims, benchmark superiority and real-world generalization claims. Their supporting supplementary evidence is reduced without narrowing these claims.

C2.justification: Section B.1's explicit qualification that HR and LCS cannot establish grounding to the true physical state disappears, together with its interpretation linking human-assessed progress correctness to navigation success. The main explanations of progress drift, memory drift and real-world transfer remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Sections A.1–A.4 and Table S1 are removed, losing detailed backbone configuration, batch sizes, frame counts, loss weight, scheduling, DAgger intervention/filtering rules, complete prompts and robot-control settings. Section 4.1 still directs readers to the absent appendix. This substantially reduces reproducibility; the promise to release code and data is unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work discussion, novelty positioning and the main bibliography are unchanged. The supplement's two references identify works already retained as main references 3 and 51, so their omission does not remove distinct cited works.

P1.justification: The retained prose, terminology and section order are unchanged. Structural edits remove the separately titled supplement and its A–B sections, while the arXiv version/date stamp changes. Section 4.1's reference to the appendix is left unresolved.

P2.justification: v2 removes the supplementary hyperparameter and progress-evaluation tables, deployment architecture diagram, simulated trajectory comparison, landmark-similarity plot and additional robot visualization. These are substantive display removals, not relocations. Main Figures 1–6, Tables 1–4 and their layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The unchanged main paper loses substantial reproduction information and direct evidence for its central grounding mechanisms. Removing Appendix A makes implementation harder to reconstruct, while deleting Table S2 and Figure S3 weakens validation of the retained claims. The dangling appendix reference further harms completeness, with no compensating methodological, evidential or explanatory improvement.
